claimsSupported.claim: The Canal #barra archive contains university-preserved evidence of public banter between recurring nicknames.

The Biano- exchange appears as a short public sequence: an initial teasing line frames him as 'galinha' / womanizer, and the following line intensifies that reputation into sexualized nickname mythmaking.
Public joking could operate as flirtatious reputation amplification inside the channel.
Male participants could amplify another male nickname's flirtatious or womanizer reputation through humor, exaggeration and sexualized banter before the broader channel audience.
Friendship ties could produce cooperative promotion: one participant elevated another, while the group bond increased the visibility and symbolic value of both.
Nickname-level mythmaking was produced through live presence and public recognition, not only through technical access roles such as Operator, Master or Founder.

analyticalReading.description: This sequence is not catalogued as mere vulgar humor. It shows a short public buildup around Biano-: first, Roooo frames him as too much of a 'galinha' / womanizer for her sister; then VaNZaN intensifies the frame by publicly elevating him through exaggerated sexualized banter. The value of the excerpt lies in showing how a flirtatious male reputation could be amplified, joked about and mythologized in real time before the wider channel audience.
analyticalReading.presenceModelRelevance: The excerpt supports the IRC-Web-Presence model by showing reputation being produced live, through public performance and audience visibility inside the channel.
analyticalReading.fraternityRelevance: The excerpt helps explain the climate of male fraternity in the channel: long-term users could publicly promote one another through joking, exaggeration and shared familiarity.
analyticalReading.coPromotionRelevance: The mechanism is not only individual self-promotion. It can be read as cooperative promotion through friendship ties: by publicly elevating a friend, the speaker reinforces the friend's desirability, flirtatious reputation and mythic status while also displaying his own intimacy, humor and position within the group. Status circulates through the bond.
analyticalReading.contextRelevance: The preceding line matters because it shows that the VaNZaN line was not isolated. It participated in a live pile-on around Biano-'s 'galinha' reputation, turning a teasing setup into public mythmaking.
analyticalReading.audienceRelevance: The promotion mattered because it happened before a mixed public audience. The channel audience turned the joke into reputational performance rather than private banter.
analyticalReading.terminologyNote: The preferred analytical term is 'flirtatious reputation amplification' or 'womanizer-reputation mythmaking'. The archive avoids specialized terminology that may be misread outside its academic context.

limitations: The exact annex/page location still needs full indexing.
This short sequence should not be generalized to all Canal #barra interactions.
The line should be interpreted with recurrence context: the involved nicknames are understood by the archive as recurring participants, but that recurrence should be source-indexed separately.
The excerpt does not prove that women were passive participants; it only supports analysis of public status performance before a mixed channel audience.
The friendship/co-promotion reading is interpretive and should be strengthened through additional examples of reciprocal public promotion among recurring participants.
The file path still contains an older term for continuity of repository history; the preferred terminology inside the record is 'flirtatious reputation amplification'.
